entries.reason: the port's own CharonMetal4CommandQueue conforms to it, so the protocol object and its method list are emitted with that class's object and the surface's rows for the protocol's members are answered by the protocol rather than by a second spelling of each method. The corpus asks for a lift and not for code: the protocol is header-ok in the SDK 26.2 dump and the 16.4 SDK this package compiles against does not declare it, so the declaration is transcribed into CharonMetalProtocols.h by tools/transcribe-protocols.py@52253c0650, facts only, exactly as every other Metal protocol the 16.4 SDK lacks is (facts/Metal/Descriptors14.md for the eleven that arrived with the 14.0 descriptors)
entries.effect: an application that holds id<MTL4CommandQueue> gets the port's own queue, NSProtocolFromString answers the name, and -conformsToProtocol: answers YES for the class. That is not a formality: check_registry holds a member row to a built object carrying that spelling, and the run of the landing gate on 2026-10-04 failed all ten Metal 4 queue rows - the eight methods and MTL4CommandQueue.device and .label - with "listed as implemented, but nothing of that name is built", because the methods were on a Charon* class and a member row naming the protocol is counted from the protocol object's method list and not from a Charon class's. The four `inert` rows did not fail because only `implemented` rows are held to it. The device probe asks ten of the members on the emulated guest and reports "metalchain: 29 check(s), 2 failure(s), 12 not answered" (facts/Metal/CommandChain26.md)
